headline: Edison's Phonograph Astonishes London Press: Dead Man's Voice Fills the Room
dispatch: London correspondents were left speechless yesterday when Thomas Edison's phonograph reproduced a recorded performance of Arthur Sullivan's The Lost Chord before a gathered press audience. The machine's brass horn carried the melody clearly across the room, proving that sound could be captured and replayed at will. It was the first time music had ever been heard from a recording device at a public demonstration.
answer: First music recording played publicly in London, 1888
